intended_object: The Hopf–Lax formula u(t,x) = inf_y (φ(y) + t·L((x−y)/t)), with initial datum φ and Lagrangian L, as in Evans §3.3.2. It is the value function of the associated control problem and the candidate solution of the Hamilton–Jacobi equation. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body `⨅ y, φ y + t * L (t⁻¹ • (x - y))` is exactly the Hopf–Lax formula. Evans states it on ℝⁿ; here it is stated on any real vector space, which is all the formula needs. Topology and norms only enter in later lemmas about semicontinuity and the cost ‖w‖^p, so the definition is at its natural generality. One limitation is that the infimum is taken in ℝ rather than in EReal. When φ or L is not bounded below, `iInf` on ℝ returns the junk value 0. The docstring says this openly, and the library's lemmas assume both functions are bounded below and t ≥ 0. With those assumptions the definition gives the true infimum. This is the usual Mathlib junk-value convention, not an error. At t = 0 the formula gives inf φ + 0, which is the documented degenerate case. Mathlib has no Hopf–Lax or general infimal-convolution definition that this duplicates.
